findings.explanation: apiserver_client_certificate_expiration_seconds is an ALPHA histogram. It records the remaining lifetime, in seconds, of client certificates presented to the API server. It is not a gauge and has no per-secret notAfter epoch, so it cannot be joined to individual secrets.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe it as a histogram (_bucket/_sum/_count) of remaining client-certificate lifetime in seconds, usable only as a fleet-level early warning (for example, a non-zero count in buckets below 7 or 30 days). It is not a source of per-secret expiry dates.

findings.explanation: Application_State was deprecated in CIM 4.12 in favour of the Endpoint datamodel. Neither Application_State nor Inventory models certificate expiry; CIM has a Certificates datamodel (All_Certificates.SSL) with ssl_end_time, ssl_subject and ssl_issuer.
findings.suggested_fix: Map openshift:certificates to the Certificates datamodel (All_Certificates.SSL.ssl_end_time, ssl_subject_common_name, ssl_issuer). Drop Application_State, and drop Inventory unless it is used for node context.

findings.explanation: The repository's Splunkbase catalogue lists app 3743 as 'Monitoring Kubernetes - Metrics and Log Forwarding' (monitoringkubernetes); the guide calls it Splunk Connect for Kubernetes. No 'Splunk Add-on for Kubernetes' exists at that ID.
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle the reference to the actual 3743 listing, or replace it with the Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Kubernetes, which the guide recommends for OpenShift.

findings.explanation: The guide names Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Kubernetes and Splunk Connect for Kubernetes (3743) for OpenShift. No Splunk_TA_kubernetes add-on appears in the grounding.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm on Splunkbase whether a Splunk_TA_kubernetes package exists. If it does not, name the Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Kubernetes plus the scripted oc exporter.

findings.explanation: The fenced SPL in detailedImplementation does not match the spl field. The spl field uses `secret_name="clusteroperator__".co_name` and `cert_subject_cn="clusteroperator:".co_name`, while the fenced copy uses strcat(). The text claims the two match exactly.
findings.quote: Fenced SPL must match the spl JSON field exactly
findings.suggested_fix: Make detailedImplementation reproduce the spl field verbatim, or remove the 'must match exactly' sentence.

findings.explanation: This is the root of the Red Hat Knowledgebase, not a specific article, so it does not support the 'certificate recovery guidance' title.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the specific OpenShift documentation for recovering from expired control-plane certificates for the supported minor version, or remove the entry.

findings.explanation: The OAuth server serving material in openshift-authentication normally uses names such as v4-0-config-system-serving-cert. 'v4-0-0-system-master-auth' does not appear to be a real secret name.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `oc get secret -n openshift-authentication` on a supported release and use the actual serving-cert secret name.

findings.explanation: The OpenShift kube-apiserver-operator auto-rotates the kube-apiserver-to-kubelet signer. Manual CSR approval is normally needed only for kubelet client or serving CSRs after a cluster has been offline. Case B and the SPL 'manual' rotation_policy class rest on this claim.
findings.quote: many leaves auto-rotate while kube-apiserver-to-kubelet signers may still need manual approvals
findings.suggested_fix: Check the OpenShift 'API server certificates' and 'Node certificates' documentation. Reword Case B to cover pending kubelet CSRs after prolonged downtime rather than manual signer rotation.

findings.explanation: 'DistIssuer' is not an OpenShift component. The service-ca-operator injects CA bundles into ConfigMaps annotated with service.beta.openshift.io/inject-cabundle.
findings.quote: verify DistIssuer still publishes valid CABundle ConfigMaps
findings.suggested_fix: Say: verify the service-ca operator still injects the CA bundle into ConfigMaps annotated service.beta.openshift.io/inject-cabundle=true.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified with only a generic reviewer handle, yet its SPL cannot run (stats inside a multisearch arm) and it misinterprets the Prometheus metric. That is not evidence of SME sign-off.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the status to draft or community until an SME has run the search against real OpenShift data and recorded the sign-off.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The fourth multisearch arm contains `stats count ... BY cluster namespace secret_name`. multisearch accepts only streaming commands in its subsearches, so the search fails to parse.

The Prometheus lane treats metric values between 1e9 and 4e9 as a notAfter epoch. apiserver_client_certificate_expiration_seconds is a histogram of remaining seconds, so bucket counts and _sum never represent an epoch. The lane yields null or meaningless expiry and one fake secret row named prom__apiserver_client_certificate_expiration_seconds.

In the ClusterOperator lane, any message matching cert|tls|rotate|expir sets a synthetic expiry of now+1d, which yields page severity. This happens even when the operator is Available=True and not Degraded, because the Degraded condition status is never checked. Routine 'rotating certificate' Progressing messages would therefore page.

The `streamstats window=20000 current=t min(...)` that produces cat_fastest_expiry depends on event order: early rows see only partial minima. Use eventstats min(days_until_expiry) BY cluster ca_bundle_kind instead.

cimSpl queries the deprecated Application_State model and uses the wrong root dataset prefixes (Application_State.*, Inventory.* rather than All_Application_State / All_Inventory). Neither model carries certificate expiry, so the query cannot support this detection. The Certificates datamodel (All_Certificates.SSL.ssl_end_time) fits the signal.

summary: The UC scopes operator-managed OpenShift PKI well and has useful case-based runbooks. However, it misreads apiserver_client_certificate_expiration_seconds as a per-certificate gauge or epoch, its SPL cannot run because a multisearch arm uses stats, it maps to the deprecated Application_State CIM model, and it misnames Splunkbase 3743.
